claims.text: The claimant's account, published in January 1989: an object that 'maneuvered around' the warhead package, 'emitted four distinct bright flashes of light at approximately the 4 cardinal compass points of its orbit', and a warhead that 'malfunctioned and tumbled out of suborbit hundreds of miles short of its target'. His own dating is uncertain: 'most probably either September 2nd, 3rd, or 15th, 1964'.

claims.text: The 1369th Photographic Squadron was based here: Robert Jacobs gives his post as 'Officer-in-Charge of Photo-optical Instrumentation in the 1369th Photographic Squadron at Vandenberg Air Force Base, California from May, 1963 to May, 1966', and the project engineer independently confirms that Jacobs 'was named the on-site commander by the 1369th Photo Squadron'.

edges.label: On-site commander at the filming; his presence, unit and role confirmed by the project engineer in print
edges.note: THE ONLY TIER 1 WITNESS-TO-CASE EDGE IN THIS CLUSTER. Jacobs published his own account in January 1989; Kingston George, the project engineer, wrote in 1993 that 'Bob was named the on-site commander by the 1369th Photo Squadron and managed the logistics of the operation at the Big Sur location', and published team photographs captioning Jacobs into and out of them. The edge carries his PRESENCE, not his interpretation.
